correctness.rationale: Because v is in its own neighborhood, the vertices with zero disagreement degree are precisely the prescribed monochromatic neighborhoods W=A∪Z, with their bits fixed by A versus Z. The others B must be covered by disagreement edges, and no such edge can touch W. Conversely every edge subset of a forest fixes a binary coloring up to one bit per component, by propagating parity along unique paths. Anchoring each marked component consumes exactly one bit, and agreement with its remaining fixed bits is exactly the stated path-parity test, including the zero-count case. Empty B has the empty edge cover; an isolated vertex of B makes the count zero. At W empty one obtains 2^c e(T). For nonempty W, adjoining a fixed set of edges incident to W covers all those vertices, and deleting that set recovers the original cover because it was confined to B. This injection gives the factor 2^-s. There is a central coloring on every component, and c disjoint K₂ components with s made monochromatic attain equality for every claimed c,s. The central-count tree recursion follows by multiplying child options and subtracting the all-child-edges-absent term when the parent edge is absent. The checker and verification reports were read, not executed; their finite cases are not the proof. The assertion depends on isolate-free forests and the specified reflexive observations.

evidence: Clique bouquets and crown graphs give exact inverse spectra including central maxima for their own graph families. In the bouquet result the center is 2∏(2^{s_i}-1); a crown has 4n distinguished noncentral fibers of size 2^{n-1}-n.

broader_coverage.reasoning: These exact but family-specific spectra do not include arbitrary forests, or imply a componentwise factor for every disjoint pair A,Z. A small common member, if any, does not imply coverage of the full result.

value.rationale: An inverse observation can conceal many subsets, and counting distinct observations does not measure this ambiguity. The formula characterizes even unrealizable label pairs, identifies a unique most ambiguous pair and quantifies the sharp multiplicity loss per affected component for an entire natural graph class. The central count also has a practical tree recurrence. The value lies in the forest-wide inverse problem and sharp comparison, not in recomputing edge covers or claiming the same encoding for cyclic graphs.
